text: The man will likely prevail because when he acquired both properties five years ago, the recorded easement merged into his single title and was extinguished. Upon selling to the purchaser two years later, no express reservation of that right-of-way existed in the warranty deed, meaning the burden never separated from the land again. Consequently, the purchaser has no legal claim to use the path once he moved onto a property where the easement had already been terminated by merger. CONFIDENCE: 95
